title: Bee or wasp sting
summary: Remove a retained stinger promptly, treat local pain, and watch for anaphylaxis.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Bee and Wasp Stings
actions: Move away from the insects. Remove a visible stinger as quickly as possible by scraping or pulling; speed matters more than the method.
Wash with soap and water. Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for up to 20 minutes at a time.

Widespread hives, swelling of the lips or tongue, throat tightness, wheezing, breathing difficulty, repeated vomiting, or fainting may be anaphylaxis: use prescribed epinephrine and call emergency services.
Get urgent help for many stings or a sting inside the mouth or throat.
Monitor local swelling. Seek medical care if swelling becomes extensive, infection develops, or symptoms persist.
prohibitions: Do not delay while choosing a stinger-removal method.
Do not scratch the site or apply toothpaste, urine, or unproven remedies.
Do not leave a person with systemic symptoms alone.

redFlags.text: Emergency warning signs selected—contact emergency services now.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for any whole-body allergic reaction, breathing problem, fainting, or numerous stings.
